title: Crayford Mojito Is a Restomodded Mini in a Bathing Suit

body_markdown:
Restomods based on the original Mini are a dime a dozen, and most builds focus[on adding power, luxury, or both](https://www.hagerty.com/media/new-car-reviews/the-david-brown-mini-remastered-oselli-edition-is-a-miniature-marvel/) to the pocket-sized classic. England-based Crayford has a completely different proposition: It’s turning the classic Mini into a fun, beach car-inspired four-seater called the Mojito that offers numerous customization options and a surprisingly (for a restomod) affordable price tag.


Available with left- or right-hand drive, the Mojito was seemingly designed to fill the gap between the standard Mini and[the Mini Moke](https://www.hagerty.com/media/new-car-reviews/the-new-moke-is-no-joke/) . Crayford removed the doors and cut out the quarter panels to open up both sides of the car so air and sunlight can enter the cabin. The roof stays in place, and it’s fixed, but a folding, Webasto-style sunroof that turns the Mojito into a quasi-convertible is standard. We’d argue that the Mini wears the buggy-like styling well; It almost looks like it was built by the factory.


Buyers can choose to keep the donor car’s paint color or select one of four options: White Sand, Beach Yellow, Surf Blue, or Custom Mojito. If the donor car is a newer Mini, you can make it look older with the optional MK1 Styling Pack.


In true beach car fashion, the Mojito comes with durable, marine-grade upholstery and non-slip Flexiteek front flooring to ensure you won’t ruin the interior if you hop in right after going for a swim. The dashboard’s layout stays close to stock, meaning what it looks like depends on the donor car’s year, but available upgrades include Android Auto compatibility and locking gloveboxes.

The base engine is a 1.3-liter four-cylinder that has been “tuned for drivability,” according to Crayford. It spins the front wheels via a four-speed manual transmission. The list of extra-cost options includes an automatic transmission ([about $2000](https://www.crayfordautomobiles.com/) ), a performance-tuned evolution of the 1.3-liter fitted with fuel injection (about $4600), and an electric drivetrain, the price of which hasn’t been released.


Built by hand from a donor car, the Crayford Mojito starts at £35,000, which represents about $46,000 at the current conversion rate. That’s reasonable considering restomods often land[with a six-digit price tag](https://www.hagerty.com/media/news/david-brown-100k-mini-remastered/) . There’s no word yet on whether the Mojito will be distributed in the United States, but the classic Mini is old enough to import, so bringing one here shouldn’t be terribly difficult.


Buying a Mojito might be difficult, however: Crayford claims availability is limited, though it hasn’t released how many it intends to build.
